experiment: two axes with no ledger entry: (A) rank (Spearman) kernel -- rank each subject's edges before building the between-subject kernel, so subjects are compared by edge-profile SHAPE; (B) lambda-bag KRR -- average the predictions of six plateau lambdas instead of picking one.
condition: published six modalities, g0.92/k150, alpha0.10, w0.05, lambda 1e-6..10 by inner 4-fold, fold-mean r, 60 seeds

verdict.lambda_bag: CATASTROPHIC: 0.6815 (-0.0511, 0/60). The lambda grid spans 1e-3..0.3 here, which straddles the regime change: standardising and averaging predictions from lambdas whose kernels have very different effective smoothness mixes a well-fit predictor with badly over- and under-regularised ones. Averaging is NOT a safe way to remove the selection step.
verdict.rank_kernel: POSITIVE: 0.7379 (+0.0054, 58/60, NB t 19.06). Above the 0.003 threshold the ledger sets.
verdict.certified_plus_rank_equal_mix: STRONGEST: 0.7383 (+0.0057, 60/60, NB t 38.76) -- every seed wins. But the 50/50 weight is hand-set, so it must clear the fold-internal gate before it is called a recipe.

mechanism: the edges are heavy-tailed (skew 0.82, excess kurtosis 2.13 on resting-state; |edge| 99.9th percentile 0.64 against a median of 0.07). A kernel built on raw values is dominated by a handful of extreme edges, which differ for reasons that are not individual differences in cognition. Ranking each subject's edges removes that leverage and compares profiles instead.
gate: see RANK_KERNEL_GATES.json -- fold-internal 2-way selection between the raw-value and rank kernels. Until that passes, both numbers are fixed-configuration observations, which is exactly the status the ledger gives 0.7382 (RELATIONAL 1/9).

_NB_T_CORRECTION_1119.note: session found the NB formula was wrong in this file's helper: it divided the variance by m AND multiplied by (1/k + n_te/n_tr), which under-corrects. Correct: var(d)*(1/m + n_te/n_tr). The t values in this file are inflated by 17.9x; the corrected values are below. Deltas and win counts are unaffected. No re-run needed -- the conversion is exact.
